components.note: 爻 (crossed, interwoven strands) — pictures a loosely woven pattern, the idea of something thin or sparse.
巾 (cloth) — a piece of loosely woven cloth gave 希 its early meaning 'sparse, rare,' which later extended figuratively to 'hope,' something rare and longed for.
⺼ (flesh/meat) — 腊 describes meat prepared as a sacrifice or preserved food.
昔 (former times, the past year) — meat ⺼ set aside for a sacrifice at year's end 昔 gave 腊 its meaning 'preserved meat,' and the name of the 12th lunar month.

example.hanzi: 希腊有很多美丽的岛屿。
example.pinyin: Xīlà yǒu hěnduō měilì de dǎoyǔ.
example.english: Greece has many beautiful islands.
example.fact: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, is a hand-cranked bronze device built around 150-100 BC that could predict eclipses and track the positions of the sun, moon, and planets. Its gearing is so sophisticated that historians consider it the world's oldest known analog computer, and nothing as complex reappeared in Europe for over a thousand years.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'
囗 (an enclosure) — a garden like 园 is an enclosed area of land.
元 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 园.

example.hanzi: 我们家后面有一个小花园。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā hòumiàn yǒu yígè xiǎo huāyuán.
example.english: There's a small garden behind our house.
example.fact: The Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew, in London, maintain living specimens of roughly one in every eight known plant species on Earth, making it one of the most complete plant collections anywhere. Its seed bank separately stores samples from over 10% of the world's wild plant species as insurance against extinction.

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.hanzi: 他四处寻找丢失的钥匙。
example.pinyin: Tā sìchù xúnzhǎo diūshī de yàoshi.
example.english: He searched everywhere for his lost keys.
example.fact: The pin-tumbler lock, still the most common design protecting doors worldwide, was patented by Linus Yale Jr. in 1861. Its core idea — a set of spring-loaded pins that must all be raised to exactly the right height by a matching key — has barely changed in over 160 years.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 订 relates to arranging something through discussion or agreement.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound distantly related to dìng, having drifted apart over time.
女 (woman) — 婚 relates to marriage, historically centered on the wife.
昏 (hūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 婚.

example.hanzi: 他们上个月订婚了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen shàng gè yuè dìnghūn le.
example.english: They got engaged last month.
example.fact: The now-standard idea of a diamond engagement ring owes much to a 1947 De Beers advertising campaign built around the slogan 'A Diamond Is Forever.' Before that campaign, diamonds were just one option among many for engagement jewelry; afterward, they became the expected default across much of the Western world.

components.note: 谷 (valley) — 豁 relates to an open gap or breach, like a valley cutting through terrain.
害 (hài) gives a sound distantly related to 豁's reading huō, having drifted apart over time.
免 began as a pictograph closely related to 兔 (rabbit) with its tail dropped — a hare slipping free of danger gave 免 its meanings 'to escape, to avoid, to be exempt from.'
木 (wood) — 权 originally meant a wooden lever or weight, later extended to 'power, authority, right.'
雚 was historically closer to guàn; the pronunciation has since shifted to quán, so the sound link is faint today.

example.hanzi: 外交官享有法律豁免权。
example.pinyin: Wàijiāoguān xiǎngyǒu fǎlǜ huòmiǎnquán.
example.english: Diplomats enjoy legal immunity.
example.fact: Diplomatic immunity was formalized internationally by the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, but the underlying idea — that a foreign envoy should not be punished for the actions of the government they represent — is far older, with roots in customs observed by ancient Greek city-states to keep channels of communication open even between rivals.

components.note: 广 depicts a lean-to shelter built against a wall or cliff, open on one side — the image behind its meaning 'wide, spacious' and its use as the 'building' radical.
扌 (hand) — the hand doing the sowing.
番 (a field marked out into plots) — seeds scattered by hand across it, giving 播 its meaning 'to sow, to spread, to broadcast.'

example.hanzi: 这个消息通过广播传遍了全国。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi tōngguò guǎngbō chuánbiànle quánguó.
example.english: This news spread across the whole country through the broadcast.
example.fact: Pittsburgh's KDKA is often credited with the first regularly scheduled commercial radio broadcast, airing results of the 1920 U.S. presidential election on the night of November 2. At the time, almost nobody owned a radio receiver, so the station is said to have loaned sets to listeners just to prove the new medium worked.

components.note: 西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
王 here is a variant of 玉 (jade), appearing once on each side of the character.
刂 (knife) — cutting a piece of jade in two, symbolizing a division into groups, gave 班 its meaning 'class, group.'
牙 is a pictograph of two interlocking molars, showing the way upper and lower teeth meet when the jaw closes — the image behind its meaning 'tooth.'
讠 (speech) — 语 relates to language, words, and speech
吾 (wú) gives a loose sound connection to 语's reading yǔ

example.hanzi: 她在大学学习西班牙语。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí Xībānyáyǔ.
example.english: She studies Spanish at university.
example.fact: Spanish has more native speakers than English worldwide, ranking second only to Mandarin Chinese. It is an official language in 20 countries across four continents, a spread that traces back to Spanish colonial expansion beginning in the late 15th century.

components.note: 戌 (a halberd/weapon) — represents armed force.
女 (woman) — force used to intimidate gave 威 its meaning 'power, might, awe-inspiring.'

士 is thought to originate as a pictograph of a ceremonial battle-axe, a symbol of rank carried by men of standing, which broadened to mean 'gentleman, scholar, soldier.' A popular but unrelated folk reading splits it into 十 (ten) plus 一 (one), someone who 'knows everything from one to ten.'
心 (heart) — jealousy and dread are both feelings of the heart.
己 (jǐ) gives the sound — a close match for jì, sharing the initial and rhyme.

example.hanzi: 他喝了一杯威士忌。
example.pinyin: Tā hēle yì bēi wēishìjì.
example.english: He drank a glass of whiskey.
example.fact: Under Scottish law, a spirit can only be labeled 'Scotch whisky' if it has been aged in oak casks for at least three years, a rule that traces back to regulations tightened during the First World War to curb the sale of harsh, immature spirits. That legal minimum still shapes how distilleries plan production today.

components.note: 厂 (a cliff shape) reflects 厌's original meaning related to a rock formation, later shifted to mean "to dislike."
犬 (quǎn) gives a sound distantly related to yàn, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) shows this describes a person's state.
卷 depicts something curled or rolled up, like a tired person curling up to rest.

example.hanzi: 我对这份工作感到厌倦了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè fèn gōngzuò gǎndào yànjuànle.
example.english: I've grown weary of this job.
example.fact: The World Health Organization formally added 'burnout' to its International Classification of Diseases in 2019, defining it as a syndrome from chronic, unmanaged workplace stress rather than a medical condition in itself. The classification was meant to help employers recognize it as an occupational issue, not a personal failing.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.hanzi: 他大声地喊了他的名字。
example.pinyin: Tā dàshēng de hǎnle tā de míngzì.
example.english: He shouted his name loudly.
example.fact: The 1883 eruption of the volcano Krakatoa is often called the loudest sound in recorded history — it was reportedly heard nearly 3,000 miles away in Rodrigues Island, and sailors 40 miles from the blast had their eardrums ruptured by the pressure wave.

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 今天的天空非常蓝。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānkōng fēicháng lán.
example.english: Today's sky is very blue.
example.fact: The sky looks blue because Earth's atmosphere scatters shorter blue wavelengths of sunlight far more than longer red wavelengths, a phenomenon known as Rayleigh scattering. On Mars, where the atmosphere is thin and dusty, the effect works differently and the daytime sky often appears butterscotch or reddish instead.

components.note: 木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅只使用本地食材。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng zhǐ shǐyòng běndì shícái.
example.english: This restaurant only uses local ingredients.
example.fact: The word 'locavore,' describing someone who tries to eat only food grown near where they live, was coined in 2005 by a small group of writers in the San Francisco Bay Area and was later named Oxford Word of the Year in 2007.

components.note: 冫 pictures ice crystals forming.
水 (water) sits beside it, together showing water turned to ice.
⺮ (bamboo) — 箱 originally described a bamboo case or chest.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 箱.

example.hanzi: 牛奶放在冰箱里。
example.pinyin: Niúnǎi fàngzài bīngxiāng lǐ.
example.english: The milk is in the refrigerator.
example.fact: Household refrigerators were a rarity for decades after their invention; even in the United States, fewer than 10% of homes owned one in 1930, and it took mass production through the 1930s and '40s to make them a standard kitchen appliance.

meanings: Long live (the king, the revolution etc)!

components.note: 万 is the simplified form of 萬, originally a pictograph of a scorpion. The character was borrowed purely for its sound to write the number 'ten thousand,' and the simplified shape preserves only an abstract trace of that original image.
The upper part of 岁 preserves a fragment of 步 (to walk, to step) from the traditional form 歲, hinting at time passing step by step.
夕 (evening) — one evening following another built up the sense of a full year passing, and by extension, a person's age.

example.hanzi: 人群高呼国王万岁。
example.pinyin: Rénqún gāohū guówáng wànsuì.
example.english: The crowd shouted 'long live the king.'
example.fact: Louis XIV of France holds the record for the longest verified reign of any monarch in history: 72 years and 110 days, having become king in 1643 at the age of four and ruling until his death in 1715.

meanings: partner (in a business or other joint venture)

components.note: 亼 (a lid, a cover) — pictures a lid coming down to close over something.
口 (an opening, here a container) — a lid fitting snugly over an opening gave 合 its meaning 'to close, to join, to fit together,' as when two matching halves meet.
亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 他们是律师事务所的合伙人。
example.pinyin: Tāmen shì lǜshī shìwùsuǒ de héhuǒrén.
example.english: They are partners at the law firm.
example.fact: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger ran Berkshire Hathaway together for more than five decades, a partnership widely regarded as one of the longest and most successful in modern corporate history, until Munger's death in 2023 at age 99.

components.note: 见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.
步 (to step, to walk) — suggests something happening again and again, one step after another.
页 (head) — repeated steps paired with a head originally suggested a furrowed brow of urgency, which settled into 频's modern sense of something recurring 'frequently.'

example.hanzi: 这个视频已经有一百万次观看。
example.pinyin: Zhège shìpín yǐjīng yǒu yìbǎiwàn cì guānkàn.
example.english: This video already has a million views.
example.fact: The first video ever uploaded to YouTube, a 19-second clip titled 'Me at the zoo,' was posted by co-founder Jawed Karim on April 23, 2005. It shows him standing in front of the elephant enclosure at the San Diego Zoo and is still viewable on the site today.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 治 relates to managing or controlling the flow of water, such as flood control.
台 (a platform, structure) — a structure used to direct and control water gave 治 its meaning 'to govern' or 'to manage.'
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'

example.hanzi: 这个城市的治安一直很好。
example.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de zhì'ān yìzhí hěn hǎo.
example.english: This city's public order has always been good.
example.fact: London's Metropolitan Police, established by Sir Robert Peel in 1829, is widely considered the model for modern civilian policing. Its officers are still nicknamed 'bobbies' after Peel, and the force's founding principle — policing by consent rather than force — influenced police departments around the world.

components.note: 牙 (tooth) — teeth piercing or boring through something, the origin of 'to pierce'
穴 (xué) gives a sound distantly related to 穿's reading chuān, having drifted apart considerably over time

The upper part of 着 is a graphic simplification that grew out of 著's top elements (艹 plus 者); over the centuries the two characters split apart, with 著 keeping 'to write' and 着 taking on 'wearing, attached to, in the process of.'
目 (eye) — an eye fixed on something conveys attention landing on or attaching to a target, echoed in 着's senses 'to touch, to arrive at, to wear.'

example.hanzi: 她的穿着总是很整洁。
example.pinyin: Tā de chuānzhuó zǒngshì hěn zhěngjié.
example.english: Her attire is always neat.
example.fact: Buttons have existed as decorative objects for over 5,000 years, but they weren't widely used as functional fasteners until buttonholes were invented in Europe around the 13th century — an innovation that also made tightly fitted clothing possible for the first time.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
买 (to buy) — 卖 (to sell) is the flip side of buying, the other half of a transaction.
买 (mǎi) gives a sound very close to mài, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他为了钱出卖了朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā wèile qián chūmàile péngyǒu.
example.english: He betrayed his friend for money.
example.fact: CIA officer Aldrich Ames sold classified information to the Soviet Union and later Russia for nearly a decade before his arrest in 1994, in one of the most damaging espionage cases in U.S. history. His disclosures are believed to have led to the deaths of at least ten American intelligence sources.

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo
讠 (speech/writing) — the act of putting words down.
己 (oneself, private) — writing down one's own private notes or memories, giving 记 its meaning 'to record, remember.'

example.hanzi: 请在地图上标记你的位置。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài dìtú shàng biāojì nǐ de wèizhi.
example.english: Please mark your location on the map.
example.fact: The Latin phrase 'hic sunt dracones' ('here be dragons'), often imagined as a common warning on old maps, actually appears on only one known historical map — the 1510 Hunt-Lenox Globe, one of the oldest surviving globes to depict the New World.

components.note: 入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 游泳可以锻炼全身的肌肉。
example.pinyin: Yóuyǒng kěyǐ duànliàn quánshēn de jīròu.
example.english: Swimming can exercise the muscles of the whole body.
example.fact: Skeletal muscle makes up roughly 40% of an average adult's total body mass, more than any other single tissue type in the human body, including bone, fat, or organs.

meanings: dedicated (to a particular field or purpose)

components.note: 叀 (a spindle or thread-reel) — pictures thread being wound onto a single spool.

寸 (a hand) — a hand turning the spindle so all the thread gathers in one place, the image behind 专's meaning 'concentrated, specialized, exclusive.' The simplified form 专 keeps only an abstracted trace of the original spindle shape.
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.hanzi: 这个实验室专门研究癌症治疗。
example.pinyin: Zhège shíyànshì zhuānmén yánjiū áizhèng zhìliáo.
example.english: This laboratory specializes in cancer treatment research.
example.fact: The first effective chemotherapy drug, nitrogen mustard, emerged from an unexpected observation: doctors noticed that soldiers exposed to mustard gas in World War II had unusually low white blood cell counts. That insight led researchers in the 1940s to test related compounds against lymphoma, launching the modern era of cancer chemotherapy.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'
禾 (grain, a rice/wheat plant) — 科 relates to sorting and measuring crops.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring grain into ordered categories gave 科 its meaning 'a branch of study' or 'a department.'

example.hanzi: 他的父亲是一名外科医生。
example.pinyin: Tā de fùqīn shì yì míng wàikē yīshēng.
example.english: His father is a surgeon.
example.fact: Ether was first used publicly as a surgical anesthetic on October 16, 1846, at Massachusetts General Hospital, in an operation now commemorated annually as 'Ether Day.' Before that demonstration, surgery meant enduring the operation fully conscious, so the discovery transformed what procedures were even possible.

components.note: 钅 (metal) shows 钢 names a type of metal.
冈 (gāng) gives the exact sound of 钢.
玨 (two connected jade pieces, representing strings) at the top shows the instrument's strings.
今 at the bottom rounds out the character's shape, giving 琴 its meaning 'a stringed instrument.'

example.hanzi: 她每天练习钢琴一个小时。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān liànxí gāngqín yí gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: She practices piano for an hour every day.
example.fact: The piano was invented around 1700 by the Italian instrument maker Bartolomeo Cristofori, who called his creation a 'gravicembalo col piano e forte' — a harpsichord-like instrument that, unlike its predecessor, could play both softly and loudly depending on how hard a key was struck.

components.note: 人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 两位领导人在联合国会面。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi lǐngdǎorén zài Liánhéguó huìmiàn.
example.english: The two leaders met at the United Nations.
example.fact: The land beneath United Nations headquarters in New York is technically international territory, purchased in 1946 with an $8.5 million donation from John D. Rockefeller Jr. — worth well over $100 million today — specifically so the fledgling organization would have a permanent home.

components.note: 女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
良 (good) — 郎 originally described a fine, well-regarded man.
阝 (a settlement, a place) — a good man 良 from a certain place 阝 gave 郎 its meaning 'a young man, a gentleman.'

example.hanzi: 电影里的邦女郎总是很神秘。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de Bāng nǚláng zǒngshì hěn shénmì.
example.english: The Bond girls in the movies are always mysterious.
example.fact: The James Bond film series began with 'Dr. No' in 1962 and has since grossed more than $7 billion worldwide, making it one of the highest-grossing film franchises ever made, spanning six different lead actors over more than 60 years.

components.note: 亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'
亻 (person) — 仇 describes a person one holds a grudge against, 'an enemy.'
九 (jiǔ) is only distantly related in sound to chóu — the connection has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他花了十年时间策划复仇。
example.pinyin: Tā huāle shí nián shíjiān cèhuà fùchóu.
example.english: He spent ten years planning his revenge.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a stone stele around 1754 BC in ancient Babylon, is one of the earliest known written legal codes to formalize proportional retribution — the principle, later summarized as 'an eye for an eye,' that a punishment should match the harm done.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) gives a hint of the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.

example.hanzi: 她大学主修数学。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué zhǔxiū shùxué.
example.english: She majored in mathematics in college.
example.fact: The number zero was developed as both a placeholder and a number in its own right by Indian mathematicians, most notably formalized by Brahmagupta around 628 AD, who also worked out rules for arithmetic involving zero and negative numbers centuries before these ideas reached Europe.

meanings: to go so far as to

components.note: 至 depicts an arrow reaching the ground after landing — arriving at a destination gave 至 its meaning 'to arrive' or 'until.'

于 is the simplified form of 於, whose oracle-bone shape is thought to depict a wooden pole or the sound of a sigh. The character was later borrowed almost entirely for its sound to serve as the grammatical preposition 'at, in, than.'

example.hanzi: 至于价格,我们可以再谈。
example.pinyin: Zhìyú jiàgé, wǒmen kěyǐ zài tán.
example.english: As for the price, we can discuss it later.
example.fact: Coined money is believed to have first appeared around 600 BC in the ancient kingdom of Lydia, in what is now western Turkey, using electrum, a naturally occurring pale gold-and-silver alloy. Standardized coinage made pricing and trading far more efficient than the barter and weighed-metal systems it replaced.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 篮 names an object often woven from bamboo, a basket.
监 (jiān) gives a sound only distantly related to lán today, having drifted apart over time.
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match

example.hanzi: 他每天晚上都去打篮球。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshàng dōu qù dǎ lánqiú.
example.english: He goes to play basketball every evening.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in December 1891 by James Naismith, a Canadian physical education instructor in Springfield, Massachusetts, who needed an indoor winter activity for his students and nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony to serve as the original goals.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — 登 relates to climbing or ascending with one's legs
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 登's reading dēng, having drifted apart over time
讠 (speech/writing) — the act of putting words down.
己 (oneself, private) — writing down one's own private notes or memories, giving 记 its meaning 'to record, remember.'

example.hanzi: 请在前台登记你的信息。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài qiántái dēngjì nǐ de xìnxī.
example.english: Please register your information at the front desk.
example.fact: Compulsory civil registration of births and deaths in England and Wales began with the Births and Deaths Registration Act of 1836, which took effect in 1837. One motivation was administrative: officials needed reliable records to enforce the country's newly reformed Poor Law system.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
寸 (a hand) — guiding the way.
巳 (a place) — the destination being pointed toward, giving 导 its meaning 'to lead, guide, direct.'

example.hanzi: 教练亲自指导每一位运动员。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn qīnzì zhǐdǎo měi yī wèi yùndòngyuán.
example.english: The coach personally guides every athlete.
example.fact: The English word 'mentor' comes from a character in Homer's 'Odyssey' — an old friend of Odysseus named Mentor, entrusted with guiding and advising his son Telemachus during Odysseus's long absence.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诊 describes a doctor asking questions and speaking with a patient to diagnose an illness.
㐱 (zhěn) gives the sound — an exact match with 诊.
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'

example.hanzi: 她在附近的诊所工作。
example.pinyin: Tā zài fùjìn de zhěnsuǒ gōngzuò.
example.english: She works at a nearby clinic.
example.fact: The Mayo Clinic grew out of a small private medical practice that Dr. William Worrall Mayo ran in Rochester, Minnesota, starting in the 1860s. It expanded rapidly after a devastating 1883 tornado forced the town to build a hospital to treat the injured, laying the groundwork for what became one of the world's largest medical centers.

meanings: (of a contagious disease etc) to spread
(of a style of clothing, song etc) popular

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates directly to 流's meaning 'to flow.'
㐬 (liú) gives the sound — 流 is also pronounced liú, an exact match.
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.

example.hanzi: 这首歌去年非常流行。
example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē qùnián fēicháng liúxíng.
example.english: This song was very popular last year.
example.fact: The 1918 influenza pandemic, often called the 'Spanish flu' even though it likely didn't originate in Spain, is estimated to have infected about 500 million people — roughly a third of the world's population at the time — making it one of the deadliest outbreaks in recorded history.

meanings: (fig.) person who has the potential to do the job

components.note: 木 (wood) — 材 originally named timber.
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 材.
米 (rice) — the grain being measured.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring out rice gave 料 its meaning 'material, to estimate, to reckon.'

example.hanzi: 这座桥使用了新型材料建造。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo shǐyòngle xīnxíng cáiliào jiànzào.
example.english: This bridge was built using new materials.
example.fact: Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice, is roughly 200 times stronger than steel by weight, yet it was first isolated in 2004 using little more than ordinary adhesive tape to peel thin flakes off a block of graphite — a discovery that earned its researchers the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics.

components.note: 扌 (hand) shows 揭 relates to an action done by hand, like lifting a cover off.
曷 (hé) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
日 (sun) — 晓 describes the sun coming up, dawn, and by extension, becoming clear.
尧 (yáo) gives a sound close to xiǎo.

example.hanzi: 获奖名单将在晚会上揭晓。
example.pinyin: Huòjiǎng míngdān jiāng zài wǎnhuì shàng jiēxiǎo.
example.english: The list of winners will be announced at the evening event.
example.fact: Nobel Prize laureates are typically informed by a phone call just minutes before the public announcement, and under Swedish law the nominating committee's internal deliberations are sealed for 50 years before historians and the public can examine them.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'

example.hanzi: 考试前她感到非常不安。
example.pinyin: Kǎoshì qián tā gǎndào fēicháng bù'ān.
example.english: She felt very uneasy before the exam.
example.fact: The 'fight-or-flight' response — the rush of adrenaline that speeds up heart rate and sharpens alertness when facing a perceived threat — was first named and described by the American physiologist Walter Cannon in the 1920s.

components.note: 日 (sun) at the bottom shows the sun low in the sky.
氏 above suggests the sun dipping out of sight, giving 昏 its meaning 'dusk, growing dark.'
辶 (to walk) — 迷 originally described losing one's way while walking, extending to 'confused, obsessed.'
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mí, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他因为车祸昏迷了三天。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi chēhuò hūnmíle sān tiān.
example.english: He was in a coma for three days because of a car accident.
example.fact: The Glasgow Coma Scale, still the standard tool doctors use worldwide to assess a patient's level of consciousness after a head injury, was developed by two neurosurgeons in Glasgow in 1974. It scores eye, verbal, and motor responses on a scale from 3 to 15.

components.note: 邦 (a nation/state) — a community bound together
巾 (a flag/cloth) — a banner people rally around to support one another
邦 (a nation/state) — a community bound together
巾 (a flag/cloth) — a banner people rally around to support one another

example.hanzi: 你能帮帮我吗?
example.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāngbāng wǒ ma?
example.english: Can you help me out?
example.fact: The emergency number 911 was chosen for the United States in 1968 specifically because it was short, easy to remember on a rotary phone, and had never been used as a telephone exchange prefix or area code anywhere in the country, so it could be dialed unambiguously nationwide.

components.note: 午 was originally a pictograph of a wooden pestle used for pounding grain. The character was later borrowed for its sound to label the seventh of the twelve earthly branches, which corresponds to the 'horse' hour and, by extension, noon.
夕 (evening/night) — the darkness that has fallen
亻 (a person) — someone moving under cover of night

example.hanzi: 他们工作到午夜才回家。
example.pinyin: Tāmen gōngzuò dào wǔyè cái huí jiā.
example.english: They worked until midnight before going home.
example.fact: Before railways forced standardization, most towns kept their own local time based on the sun, so noon in one city could be several minutes off from noon in a neighboring one. Britain adopted a single 'Railway Time' in 1840 to keep train schedules consistent, though it wasn't made the legal standard nationwide until 1880.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'

关 is the simplified form of 關, which showed 門 (a door) barred shut by a crossbar threaded through it — a door sealed tight, giving the meaning 'to close, to bar.' That image of two things linked by a bar extended to 'relation, connection,' while a barred passage through the mountains gave the meaning 'a strategic pass.' The simplified 关 keeps only an abstracted crossbar-and-legs shape, dropping the door radical entirely.

example.hanzi: 吸烟与肺癌密切相关。
example.pinyin: Xīyān yǔ fèi'ái mìqiè xiāngguān.
example.english: Smoking is closely linked to lung cancer.
example.fact: The 1964 U.S. Surgeon General's report was the first major government publication to formally conclude that smoking causes lung cancer, based on a review of more than 7,000 scientific studies by an independent advisory committee.

components.note: 身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.
木 (wood) — 材 originally named timber.
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 材.

example.hanzi: 她通过跑步保持好身材。
example.pinyin: Tā tōngguò pǎobù bǎochí hǎo shēncái.
example.english: She stays in good shape by running.
example.fact: The marathon's official distance of 26.2 miles was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics so the race could start at Windsor Castle and finish directly in front of the royal viewing box in the stadium — a scheduling decision, not any ancient Greek precedent, which is a common misconception about the distance's origin.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讽 relates to speaking, in this case mocking through words.
风 (fēng) gives a sound close to fěng, sharing the same initial and rhyme with a different tone.
刂 (knife) — 刺 describes the action of piercing or stabbing with something sharp.
朿 (cì) gives the sound — an exact match with 刺's reading cì.

example.hanzi: 这部电影充满了政治讽刺。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng chōngmǎnle zhèngzhì fěngcì.
example.english: This movie is full of political satire.
example.fact: Jonathan Swift's 1729 essay 'A Modest Proposal,' which satirically suggested that impoverished Irish families sell their children as food to wealthy landlords, remains one of the most studied examples of sustained satire in English literature — a piece meant not literally but to expose the cruelty of contemporary economic policy.

components.note: Ice — related to the character's early sense of cold.
Gives the sound líng, matching the character's reading.
日 (sun) — 晨 describes the time when the sun first rises, 'early morning.'
辰 (chén) gives the sound — an exact match with 晨.

example.hanzi: 他凌晨四点就起床跑步了。
example.pinyin: Tā língchén sì diǎn jiù qǐchuáng pǎobùle.
example.english: He got up at 4 a.m. to go running.
example.fact: Human core body temperature typically reaches its lowest point of the day between about 4 and 5 a.m., a low in the circadian rhythm that also coincides with when most people feel the strongest biological pull toward sleep, regardless of how much rest they've had.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 侮 concerns how one person treats, or mistreats, another.
每 (měi) — originally a pictograph of a woman with an elaborate headdress; here it anchors 侮's reading wǔ, the two pronunciations having drifted apart over the centuries.
辰 (originally a hand-held clam-shell blade used for cutting crops) — associated with the hard, humble labor of farming.
寸 (a hand) — a hand doing menial farm labor was, in ancient social hierarchy, considered demeaning, giving 辱 its meaning 'to insult, to disgrace, to humiliate.'

example.hanzi: 他在公开场合侮辱了对手。
example.pinyin: Tā zài gōngkāi chǎnghé wǔrǔle duìshǒu.
example.english: He insulted his opponent in public.
example.fact: Alexander Hamilton's fatal 1804 duel with Aaron Burr began after Hamilton refused to retract insulting remarks he had made about Burr's character. Dueling to defend one's honor after a public insult was still considered acceptable in parts of early 19th-century America, even though it was already illegal in the state where the duel took place.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
山 (mountain) forms the top of the character.
厂 depicts a cliff or overhang — combined with 山 above, suggesting the steep edge of land meeting water, giving 岸 its meaning 'bank, shore.'

example.hanzi: 他们沿着海岸散步。
example.pinyin: Tāmen yánzhe hǎi'àn sànbù.
example.english: They walked along the coast.
example.fact: Norway's coastline, once every fjord and offshore island is measured, stretches for more than 100,000 kilometers — long enough to circle the Earth over twice — even though the country's land area is only about 385,000 square kilometers.

components.note: 亚 (here a stylized shape related to advancing in rank) sits above.
日 (sun, day) below anchors the meaning in time, giving 晋 its sense 'to advance, to promote.'
纟 (thread) — 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread, extended to 'grade, level, rank.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 级 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这支球队晋级了半决赛。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì jìnjíle bànjuésài.
example.english: This team advanced to the semifinals.
example.fact: The FIFA World Cup has expanded its format several times since 1930; the 2026 tournament, co-hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada, will be the first edition to include 48 national teams instead of the 32 that competed in every tournament from 1998 through 2022.

components.note: 十 (here a straight vertical line) — 直 pictures something drawn perfectly straight.
目 (eye) — looking directly and steadily with the eye gave 直 its meaning 'straight' or 'direct.'
见 (to see, perceive) — relates to 觉's meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive.'
⺍ is a small graphic element serving as the phonetic hint, though its link to jué's modern sound has faded after centuries of change.

example.hanzi: 她的直觉总是很准。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhíjué zǒngshì hěn zhǔn.
example.english: Her intuition is always accurate.
example.fact: Psychologist Daniel Kahneman's 'System 1 and System 2' framework, popularized in his 2011 book 'Thinking, Fast and Slow,' describes intuition as a fast, automatic mode of thought that runs alongside a slower, more deliberate form of reasoning. Kahneman had already won the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2002 for related work on decision-making.

components.note: 亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 政府就此事作出了正式回应。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jiù cǐshì zuòchūle zhèngshì huíyìng.
example.english: The government made a formal response to this matter.
example.fact: The system of checks and balances written into the U.S. Constitution in 1787 was heavily influenced by the French philosopher Montesquieu's 1748 treatise 'The Spirit of the Laws,' which argued that dividing government power among separate branches was necessary to prevent any one part from becoming tyrannical.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
罒 (net) — relates to 罗's original meaning 'net for catching birds,' extended to 'to gather, collect' and used today as a common Chinese surname.

example.hanzi: 保罗是我最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Bǎoluó shì wǒ zuìhǎo de péngyǒu.
example.english: Paul is my best friend.
example.fact: The name Paul derives from the Latin 'Paulus,' meaning 'small' or 'humble,' originally used as a Roman family name (cognomen) rather than a given name. Despite its modest original meaning, it has remained one of the most consistently popular male names across the Western world for close to two thousand years.
